To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the autonomic nervous system (ANS) is impaired following acute spinal cord injury, and that the ANS impairment is more severe in tetraplegic than in paraplegic patients.
spinal cord injury impairs autonomic control of blood pressure, as demonstrated by lower baroreflex gain, decreased baroreflex effectiveness, and decreased engagement of baroreflex sequences.
spinal cord injury impairs the autonomic control of blood pressure and heart rate in response to head up tilt.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the autonomic control of blood pressure regulation in human subjects with spinal cord injuries (SCI) in response to orthostatic stress.
the mechanisms underlying the loss of orthostatic tolerance in spinal cord injury (SCI).
the mechanisms underlying cardiovascular control and the effects of spinal cord injury on cardiovascular regulation.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
autonomic regulation of cardiovascular function in response to head up tilt in AB, PAR, and TETRA is different, and that this difference may contribute to orthostatic intolerance following SCI.
autonomic control of BP is impaired after spinal cord injury and that this impairment is more pronounced in tetraplegic compared with paraplegic individuals.
spinal cord injury leads to a loss of sympathetic outflow to the vasculature, and that loss is the primary cause of orthostatic intolerance in these patients.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

autonomic control of BP in human is not only regulated via the baroreflex but also by other reflexes, including the cardiopulmonary and the muscle reflexes, and that the spinal cord injury results mainly in a decreased stimulation of arterial and cardiopulmonary baroreceptors.
spinal cord injury impairs the cardiovascular response to orthostatic stress by disrupting the neural pathways that control arterial pressure and heart rate.
the spinal cord injury causes a decrease in stimulation of arterial baroceptors, less engagement of feedback regulation and diminished vasomotion.
The main takeaway from our work is that
spinal cord injury (SCI) results in decreased stimulation and feedback control of arterial baroreflexes and diminished vasomotion.
autonomic control of the cardiovascular system is impaired in individuals with spinal cord injury and that this impairment is related to the level of injury.
autonomic control of BP and HR is severely impaired following spinal cord injury and is further compromised by orthostatic stress.
